title: fix(lint): translation-target-unknown reads navigation CONTRIBUTED into an app, so a locale key for a contributed item is no longer an orphan whose remedy deletes it
body:
Fixes #18203

Clause-②: no — this PR puts no new key on any published payload and grows no public face. It widens what a lint rule READS (one module-private helper, `contributedNavItemsByApp`), and that is measured rather than asserted: the diff adds zero `export` lines, `packages/lint/src/index.ts` is untouched, and the helper is not exported, so nothing new reaches `dist/index.d.ts`. No existing judgement is removed either — 3 files, +342/-0, nothing deleted.

`translation-target-unknown` built the `apps.APP.navigation.ITEM` universe from the app's authored `navigation` array alone. An item injected by another package through `manifest.navigationContributions` (ADR-0029 D7, ADR-0130) is never in that array, so every locale key for it was reported as naming an item *"which app X does not declare"* — at `error` since 17.4.0 (#16310), with the remedy *"Match the key to the navigation item's `id`, or drop it."*

⚠️ **Following that remedy deletes a translation the runtime honours.** That is what makes this class (c) rather than a nit: the advice is not merely noisy, it is actively destructive.

| measured downstream (`objectstack-ai/hotcrm` `be11c07`, pin 17.4.0) | |
| :-- | :-- |
| `os build` | **15** findings — 5 contributed items x 3 non-default locales |
| `GET /api/v1/meta/app?id=crm_enterprise` | returns all 5 items, `zh-CN` labels **resolved** from the app's own pack |

## Reproduced here first, then shown gone

Nine cases in `validate-translation-references.test.ts`. Against unmodified `origin/main` source they are red; the false positive comes back verbatim:

```
hint:     "Match the key to the navigation item's `id`, or drop it. Declared navigation ids: group_sales, group_service, nav_leads."
message:  Translations are keyed to navigation item "nav_case", which app "crm_enterprise" does not declare.
severity: error
```

## The fix shape, and why this one

The universe now folds in every contribution aimed at the app, walked by **the same `walkNav`** a declared subtree gets — so this widens what the population *means*, not what one check site tolerates, and the membership test, `suggest()` and the `Declared navigation ids:` hint all read the one merged population.

**⛔ The runtime fold is deliberately not imported, and that was measured, not assumed.** `applyNavContributions` is a `SchemaRegistry` method in `@objectstack/objectql`; `@objectstack/lint` declares `@objectstack/spec` and, in its own `description`, *"never on a runtime"*. `os build` reaches the engine lazily for the neighbouring **group** question (`cli/src/utils/nav-contribution-groups.ts`), whose header records why that check could not live in a lint rule at all.

⭐ **A union is faithful anyway, because of a property of the fold rather than an assurance about it.** Reading `registry.ts` `applyNavContributions`: a `group` that resolves receives the items; a `group` naming nothing records `nav_contribution_group_missing` and appends them at the app top level; an omitted `group` appends at the top level too. `NavigationContributionSchema`'s header states the same from the schema side. **Every branch pushes.** The fold chooses *where* an item lands and never *whether*, so the set of addressable ids is invariant under it — and "is this id addressable?" is the only question this rule asks. Re-running the placement would pull a runtime in to compute a set the placement cannot change. All three placements are pinned side by side so the invariant cannot quietly stop holding.

**Both carriers are read**, because a stack in hand has two shapes and the rule table runs over both:

- `packages[].manifest.navigationContributions` — the ADR-0130 D4 artifact entry, reached exactly the way `validateObjectReferences`' `artifactProvidedObjectNames` reaches sibling objects (#16611). This is the shape the **per-package leg** needs (`compile.ts` step 3b-ii): the app's owner declares no contribution of its own, and the union run above it de-duplicates, so a fix reading only the union would leave that leg reporting the finding alone.
- `manifest.navigationContributions` — the stack's own `StackSchema.manifest`, where a single-`defineStack` project's contributions live. `os validate` judges only the union stack.

Both are read unconditionally — a deliberate difference from `collectNavGroupInputs`, whose either/or exists to stop one **diagnostic** being emitted twice. The output here is set membership, where a duplicate is free and a miss is the defect being repaired.

## ⭐ The control — this must not trade a false positive for a blind spot

Same stack, one key nothing contributes: still an `error`, still carrying `translation-target-unknown`, its path and its message. A contribution aimed at app **B** does not make its ids addressable under app **A**. And the contributed ids join the population the hint enumerates, so the remedy an author is handed now lists what they may actually key to.

## What this still cannot see, stated rather than implied

Contributions registered **imperatively** by plugin code (`engine.registerAppNavContribution` from a plugin's `init`) are not metadata, and no static rule can read them — that is the population `pnpm check:app-nav-i18n` has to boot a composition to judge (see its header, and `#5750`). A locale key for one of those is still reported here.

## File face (measured)

```
.changeset/18203-translation-target-contributed-nav.md     |  27 +
packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.test.ts  | 216 +
packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts       |  99 +
3 files changed, 342 insertions(+), 0 deletions
```

`packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts` is **untouched** — confirmed before starting, as the dispatch required, since a sibling card in this batch routes through it.

## Verification — all readings at `b25d1856f6`, exit codes captured by redirect-then-`$?`, never through a pipe

| run | result |
| :-- | :-- |
| the 9 new cases, unmodified source | **9 failed** — the false positive, verbatim above |
| the 9 new cases, with the fix | **9 passed** |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` | **103 files, 3839 passed**, 5 skipped, exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` | exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit` + `check:test-typecheck`, debt ledger held) |
| `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/lint^...' build` | exit 0 (dependency closure, built before anything was judged) |
| `eslint . --no-inline-config` — **whole repo, not narrowed** | **6790 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings**, exit 0 |
| derived gate families (`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`) | **60 derived / 60 run**, reconciled with recorded exit codes |

**Ablation, from the committed state.** Deleting the one fold line, proven on disk (marker `grep -c` 1 to 0; blob `ca631c62` to `0c2bdb91`) reds **8 of the 9**. The ninth is the app-B control, which asserts a finding *is* raised and therefore passes in both worlds — recorded as such rather than counted as evidence. Restored with `git checkout HEAD -- PATH` and proven byte-identical (blob back to `ca631c62`, `git diff HEAD` empty). No build is involved: the test imports the rule by relative specifier, so the mutation is the resolved subject.

**Changeset reach, measured with both controls** — subject symbol `contributedNavItemsByApp` hits 4 files under `dist/` (a `files[]` entry); positive control `translation-target-unknown` hits the same 4; negative control, a test-only local, hits 0. The change ships, so `skip-changeset` is not available and `.changeset/18203-translation-target-contributed-nav.md` carries a `patch`.

### NOT MEASURED (3 of 60) — declared, not silently skipped

`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure` and `check:type-check-debt` each exited **3 = PREREQUISITE NOT MET**: they load built entry points across the workspace (28 dependency packages for the last one) and a whole-repo build is CI's run, not this round's. That is neither a pass nor a failure. The half of `check:type-check-debt` that this diff could actually move was measured: `packages/lint`'s own ledger held green under a **built** closure.

## Acceptance notes

⚠️ **`pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs` exits 1 in this worktree, and it is not this diff.** Isolated to one variable: the gate descends the real filesystem (`readdirSync`), and it reds only when the gitignored build output `packages/spec/dist/` exists on disk. With the diff present and that directory moved aside it exits **0**; on the shared checkout (no diff, no `dist`) it exits **0**; with the diff present and `dist` restored it exits **1**. Its complaint names `packages/cli/test/init-created-files-summary.e2e.test.ts` descending `packages/spec/dist/` — neither path is in this diff. Reported, not repaired here.

Two further findings, both the same class (c) as this card on a **different rung**, both measured and both left alone deliberately — each needs a fix whose shape is not the one pinned here:

1. **The object rung.** A locale key for a field added by `objectExtensions[]` (the declared cross-package field-injection surface, `stack.objectExtensions`, target key `extend`) is reported as an orphan at `error`: `translations[0]["zh-CN"].objects.crm_lead.fields.sla_tier`, remedy *"Point the key at a declared field, or drop it"*. The rule mentions `objectExtensions` **0** times. Same trap, and the fold surface is wider (fields, views, actions, sections, tabs, validations), so it is not the mechanical twin of this change.
2. **The app-name rung, in the per-package leg.** A *contributor* package that ships the labels for its own contributed items is told app `crm_enterprise` is one *"which this stack does not define"*, remedy *"Match the key to an app's `name`, or drop it."* Widening that means widening which app names a package may translate — a resolution-context decision of the kind #16611 took at director level for object names, not a widening to make in passing.

**Measured, and the reason this PR does not widen further.** Live injection-into-another-package surfaces on `ManifestSchema`: `navigationContributions` (this card) and `contributes.kinds`, which registers a metadata-kind id the translation rule has no universe for and never visits. Every other member of `contributes` — `menus`, `themes`, `translations`, `actions`, `drivers`, `fieldTypes`, `functions`, `routes`, `commands`, `events` — is a `retiredKey` tombstone typed `never` under ADR-0049, as are top-level `capabilities` and `extensions`. **The navigation population is a population of one**, so there is nothing else here to widen to.
